title: L3 — one process model, two configurations (Exercise 3)

state_keys.messages: the dialog, append only (say() adds one)
state_keys.expected: the slot the form asked for last turn — the router reads it
state_keys.order_id: set by order_placement once POST /order answered

router.purpose: Decides which component handles this turn: the slot we asked for last turn wins, then an ordering phrase, then a menu name, then help.
router.failure: No rule matched -> help, never a guess.

pizza_recognition.purpose: Utterance -> a pizza from the live menu (name + id). Static configuration: the iteration-1 rule; LLM configuration: the service call with that rule as its fallback.
pizza_recognition.failure: Nothing recognised -> no slot written; the form asks again.

address_recognition.purpose: Utterance -> a complete address (street, house number, city), validated by the Pizza API. Same seam as the pizza recognizer.
address_recognition.failure: Incomplete or undeliverable -> no slot written, never half an address.

order_form.purpose: Asks for the first missing slot — at most one question per turn — and sets `expected` so the router knows where the next answer belongs.
order_form.failure: Nothing missing -> says nothing and lets the order through.

order_placement.purpose: POST /order — the only side effect this process has on the world.
order_placement.failure: The API refuses -> the error travels as a message, not as a crash.

confirmation.purpose: The closing message with the order id, and the end of the dialog.

help.purpose: What we say when no rule understood the utterance.

examples.label: Say hello
examples.shows: no ordering intent -> the help node answers (iteration 1, slide 1.x)

examples.label: Order by name
examples.shows: the router sees an ordering phrase, pizza_recognition fills two slots

examples.label: Just the menu word
examples.shows: an ordering phrase without a pizza -> the form asks which one

examples.label: Answer the pizza question
examples.shows: `expected` routes the turn straight to pizza_recognition

examples.label: Pizza we do not have
examples.shows: defined failure: no slot written, the form repeats the question

examples.label: Give the address
examples.text: deliver it to 5 Rue Michelet, Saint-Étienne
examples.shows: address_recognition + validation by the Pizza API, then the order is placed

examples.label: Half an address
examples.shows: no house number, no city -> nothing is written; there is no half address

examples.label: Outside the delivery area
examples.shows: the API decides the delivery area, not the code

examples.label: The lecture sentence (LLM)
examples.text: can I order the four-cheese one to number 5 in the Rue Michelet here in Saint-Étienne?
examples.shows: one sentence, both slots — works in the LLM configuration, falls back to the rule in the static one
